newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus prepares for bicommunal concert.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus prepares for bicommunal concert.

text.p: A United Nations sponsored bicommunal concert in divided Cyprus is scheduled to go ahead on Monday night amid unprecedented security measures, authorities said.

"We have received excellent cooperation from police and all necessary security measures are in place," said Waldemar Rokoszewski, spokesman for UNFICYP, the United Nations Peacekeeping Force on the divided island.
"We expect everything will go well," he added.

Pop stars Burak Kut of Turkey and Sakis Rouvas of Greece will play in U.N.-policed no man's land in the capital Nicosia on Monday night in a concert which has sparked criticism from factions, mainly right wing ones, on both sides of the divided island.

For some Greek Cypriot groups, a bicommunal concert is grossly insensitive for coming just months after the brutal killings of fellow countrymen by Turks or Turkish Cypriots on the ceasefire line last year.
The island has been divided since Turkish forces invaded the north in 1974 in response to a brief coup engineered by the military ruling Greece.
Two Greek Cypriot groups plan a protest just a mile away from the venue of the concert, while a far-right Turkish Cypriot group has also criticised the concert.

Police cordoned off about one square mile around the abandoned football pitch where the concert is scheduled with barbed wire. Around 500 officers will be on duty to ensure the concert goes ahead smoothly, a spokesman said.
Rouvas kept everybody guessing until the last minute whether he would be at the concert, arriving on the island early on Monday in a private jet.
At midday, however, Rouvas made his first appearance after a briefing from senior police officers at a courthouse close to the concert venue.

Dressed casually in faded jeans and a t-shirt and wearing sunglasses, Rouvas -- used to screaming crowds of female fans -- appeared unfazed at the furore, of a completely different nature, that his presence has caused.
He was mobbed by a group of journalists outside the court but refused to answer any questions and just smiled.
